storage.formal: existing scene/default.ess XML v1 and design/main.sgendesign stay readable; no forced new ESS internal format
storage.authority: one physical document = one session authority. An ESS includes work/architecture/design as one composite physical doc. Embedded design is projection of that ESS; independently opened .sgendesign has separate session; no silent dual write/sync.
storage.versions: candidate immutable prior versions in .sgenaxis/document-versions/<documentUuid>/<rawDigest>; journal .sgenaxis/document-transactions/<requestUuid>.json; exact storage mechanics gated by shared commit adapter review
storage.commit_point: formal document atomic replace is the single-file publish point. Version/journal supports rollback/recovery; never make a hidden pointer authoritative while showing an old ESS as saved.
storage.history: WORK in-memory per-open-session history, not durable Undo; formal save never clears history implicitly. Close/reopen starts empty history.
storage.baselines: formal content digest and recovery content digest independent; raw-byte disk digest separately detects outside edits; revision increases even Undo; dirty compares semantic digest to formal baseline, not revision counters.

canonicalization.ESS: HOST adapter parses supported v1 and maps to domain-owned canonical payload; preserve all unknown supported extension trees/attrs or refuse before mutation. Existing packet tree capture is read-only and may lose XML comment/source formatting; cannot use it as a lossless serializer without new contract tests.
canonicalization.semantic: Exclude selection/focus/playback/viewport and volatile savedAt only at explicitly approved fields; never strip arbitrary user fields by name. Include actual nodes, relations, bindings, asset versions and restrictions.
canonicalization.hashing: HOST trusted codec computes semantic hash of normalized payload; UI digest not trusted. Original raw bytes/hash kept for exact file rollback and external edit detection. WORK holds Vec<u8> immutable canonical payload and typed refs, not serde_json/OS types.
canonicalization.clear: proposal ESS clear removes work tasks, architecture elements, design children/bindings/asset refs, retains format/identity and required root scaffold; standalone design clears only its document. Preview lists all sections; cannot clear project definition or other physical docs.

transactions: validate server writer/session/revision → prepare immutable before/after + pins + reserved history → single content swap → publish one history; failures restore before and add no history

captureR+semantic digest → encode outside UI → acquire OS write lease → check old raw digest → stage/sync+retained old version → replace formal file → acknowledge only capturedR; R+1 remains dirty; no postcommit fallible metadata can fake rollback

validate current expected revision/after digest → restore before content, refs, binding restrictions → increment revision, history to redo → release only new unreferenced assets; roots include retained snapshots/undo/transactions
capture revision/action → choice; cancel remains; discard explicit; save waits success for exact leaving revision, new edit invalidates token; native exit follows same flow

asset_retention_contract.status: PROPOSED_SHARED_CONTRACT; M05 implementation outside M04 envelope
asset_retention_contract.signature: trait AssetRetentionPort { fn reserve(&self, owner: PinOwner, versions: &[AssetVersionRef]) -> Result<PinSetId, AssetError>; fn replace(&self, owner: PinOwner, expected: PinSetId, versions: &[AssetVersionRef]) -> Result<PinSetId, AssetError>; fn release(&self, owner: PinOwner, expected: PinSetId) -> Result<(), AssetError>; }
asset_retention_contract.ownership: M05 owns registry; PinOwner=(projectUuid,documentUuid,sessionUuid,kind,operationId); kind Live|Undo|Capture|Transaction; immutable pin set ids are server-issued
asset_retention_contract.release: release only removes named owner roots; physical GC never performed by M04; unknown remaining roots are retained
asset_retention_contract.failure: reserve failure before mutation leaves content/history unchanged; later release failure retains excess pins and reports cleanup pending without invalidating committed content
